title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed, mimeographed page (p. 43, 'n° 382') of a Bourbaki draft, apparently from the drafts behind 'Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats'. Grothendieck evidently reused it as scrap paper: the handwritten neighbouring pages about Lubin–Tate groups and Tate's Hodge–Tate decomposition are unrelated to it. The typed text, section 4.13 'Affaiblissement de structure', works over K = R and runs as follows.

(1) It sets I = {1, 2, ..., ∞, ω}, ordered by n < ∞ < ω, where ω means real-analytic.

(2) 4.13.1: for r ≤ s, a C^s manifold X carries a unique C^r structure X_r whose charts include all charts of the given atlas. This is the underlying (forgetful) C^r structure. It is transitive, (X_r)_{r'} = X_{r'}, and it commutes with products and with fibre products under the hypotheses of 4.11.3. A chart c at a gives isomorphisms θ_c : R^n → T_a(X) and θ'_c : R^n → T_a(X_r). The composite θ'_c∘θ_c^{-1} does not depend on c, because changes of chart act through the same Jacobian in both cases. This identifies the two tangent spaces.

(3) 4.13.2: a map f : X → X' between a C^s and a C^{s'} manifold is called C^r, for r ≤ inf(s, s'), if it is a morphism X_r → X'_r. Being C^r implies being C^{r'} for r' ≤ r, and tangent maps are compatible under these identifications. Since being a submersion, immersion or subimmersion depends only on the tangent maps (and r ≥ 1), these notions are independent of r. The text then starts the convention of saying simply that f is a submersion, etc.

This is standard foundational material on change of differentiability class.
errors: Minor typo in the original: 'n = dim_x(X)' should be dim_a(X), since the point is called a.
Not an error but worth noting: the claim that submersion/immersion/subimmersion are independent of r relies on r ≥ 1. This is guaranteed because I starts at 1; C^0 is excluded.

ideas.what: Weakening (forgetful functor) of a C^s / analytic manifold structure to C^r, with uniqueness, transitivity, compatibility with products and fibre products
ideas.modern_name: Underlying C^r structure / restriction of differentiability class
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard foundations (Whitney era, 1930s); written up by Bourbaki
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats (1967/1971), section on 'affaiblissement de structure'. Grothendieck's own authorship of this draft is unsure.

ideas.what: Canonical identification of tangent spaces of X and X_r, and invariance of tangent maps and of the submersion/immersion/subimmersion conditions under weakening
ideas.modern_name: Tangent space independent of smoothness class

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki draft page on routine manifold foundations, reused as scrap paper. It has no connection to the handwritten Lubin–Tate / Hodge–Tate notes on the neighbouring pages and contains nothing unpublished or novel.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed (a Bourbaki mimeograph 'n° 382', p. 43), not handwritten; the pencil '52' in the bottom left margin is the archive foliation number.
'n = dim_x(X)' matches the image, but it is a typo in the original for dim_a(X).
In 4.13.2 the image reads 'resp. une immersion, une subimmersion'; this is consistent with the transcription.
